verdict: Spend collapsed to $3.85 on the final day from a $13.63 daily average — the PCOS/postpartum campaign is effectively paused.
diagnosis: Facebook is your only tracked channel this period, with $2,330 spent and no visible leads, bookings, or local presence data to judge return.

signals.headline: Spend fell 72% to $3.85 daily
signals.detail: Latest day spend dropped from the $13.63 daily average, suggesting the campaign hit a budget cap or was throttled.

signals.headline: $2,330 spent across 28 days
signals.detail: One active campaign targeting PCOS and postpartum personas. No lead or conversion data flowing back to measure outcome.

signals.headline: Zero visibility on 4 channels
signals.detail: No Google Business Profile, organic social, CRM pipeline, or top performer data. Impossible to confirm leads are converting to trials.

signals.headline: Single campaign carries 100% of spend
signals.detail: No creative or audience diversification. One ad fatigue cycle or policy flag could zero out your pipeline overnight.

benchmark.label: Benchmark
benchmark.body: US health and fitness leads on Facebook run a median of $27 in 2026. Boutique and personal training studios skew higher at $32–$52. Fitness conversion rate averages roughly 8% on Meta lead campaigns.

seasonal.label: Seasonal
seasonal.body: Fitness cost per lead swings sharply month to month. September 2025 hit the yearly high near $61 before easing. Expect auction pressure to stay elevated through fall before January resolution season.

competitor.label: Competitor
competitor.subheader: Boutique studios winning on niche community
competitor.body: Studio check-ins rose 27% year-over-year versus 1% for big-box gyms. Niche positioning — like postpartum or PCOS — is exactly what boutique winners are doing. Your targeting matches the trend.

recommendations.title: Investigate why daily spend dropped to $3.85
recommendations.detail: Check for budget caps, billing issues, or disapprovals. A 72% drop on the final day usually means the account is throttled, not that demand vanished.

recommendations.title: Connect lead tracking before spending more
recommendations.detail: Without CRM or form submission data, $2,330 is unmeasurable. Consider wiring lead events back so cost per lead can be benchmarked against the $27 fitness median.

recommendations.title: Test a second creative angle alongside PCOS/postpartum
recommendations.detail: One campaign is a single point of failure. Worth testing a short vertical video with a specific trial offer to protect against fatigue.
